---
title: "Session 16 guided lab"
subtitle: "Models, validation, and course review"
---

Work in **BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj**. Copy the starter from the separate course clone
into `work/session16/`: [Quarto](starter/practical-lab.qmd) or [R Markdown](starter/practical-lab.Rmd).
All inputs are synthetic.

## Tasks following the lecture

1. **Define and fit the analysis** — Specify the model sbp_12 ~ sbp_0 + age + arm. Define complete cases using those model variables, retain excluded IDs, and set Control as the reference. Fit with na.fail, extract an estimate/interval table, and check the analysis count. Inspect the supplied model-matrix check.
2. **Predict and diagnose** — Construct new_people with baseline SBP 140 and 155, ages 55 and 65, and Control and Treatment respectively. Compare mean-response confidence intervals with individual prediction intervals. Create an ID-linked diagnostic table and inspect residual and influence plots.
3. **Construct checked folds** — Return to all 80 participants in trial, including the three missing baseline values. Use the supplied make_folds() to create five folds stratified by arm. Check unique IDs, fold counts, and disjoint training/assessment IDs. Trace one split before repeating it.
4. **Predict held-out participants** — Complete cv_predict(data, fold) using the scaffold. Within each fold, estimate baseline imputation from training rows only, fit the regression, and predict assessment rows. Preserve one finite prediction per participant. Compare pooled RMSE with a training-mean benchmark using identical folds.
5. **Audit leakage and validation design** — Compare with deliberately global imputation using the same folds. Explain the information leak regardless of the direction of the RMSE difference. State how splits change for repeated visits, a new clinic, or future observations. Repeated-fold sensitivity is an optional extension.
6. **Prepare a reproducible handoff** — Save the coefficient table, ID-linked held-out predictions and folds, RMSE comparison, analysis bundle, and sessionInfo. Verify the saved bundle can be read back. Document the separate complete-case model and imputed prediction workflow, seeds, inputs, and entry point.

## Course recap

Use the Sessions 0–16 course map to connect data preparation, reliable code,
statistical evidence, and reproducible reporting. Complete the workflow audit
and explain how earlier skills support this analysis. Broader numerical tools
remain a brief overview with optional practice.

## In-class route and follow-up

Trace one model and one training/assessment split together. Complete the scaffolded CV loop and checks in class. Finish the leakage explanation and reproducible handoff afterward. Binary prediction, numerical methods, and text parsing are optional and are not required for this core lab.

## Exit evidence

Submit the source and rendered report with results, checks, interpretation, and
an AI-use disclosure. Identify the analysis sample or resampling unit for each result.
